# VexOS AI assistant: remaining work plan

Repo: vexos-ai. Last updated: 2026-10-31. Owner: the user.
Put this file at `.github/docs/subagent_docs/remaining_work_plan.md`. Claude Code works through it and marks items off.

---

## 1. How to work through this file (Claude Code: read this first)

1. Work on ONE item at a time, in order, inside the current phase. Skip any item whose "Needs" is not met.
2. Read the item's "Read first" files before you start.
3. Items marked **USER** are for the user to do. Items marked **DECISION** need the user's answer. You do not do these and you do not guess the answer. Ask with AskUserQuestion, or skip and say why.
4. Mark off an item only when its verification passed:
   - Change `[ ]` to `[x]` and add `— done YYYY-MM-DD: one line on what changed`.
   - Partly done: use `[~]` and say exactly what is missing.
   - Blocked: use `[!]` and say what blocks it.
   - Add one line to the Log at the bottom for every item you touch.
5. Stop and ask before any change to: nix/policy.nix, the core's safety behaviour, docs/contract.md, or the CI workflow, unless the item says it is allowed.
6. If something you find contradicts this plan, stop and tell the user. Do not quietly change the plan.
7. Reports to the user: short, plain language. No shorthand without explaining it.

### Scope rule (applies to every item)

- Do not create, modify or delete anything outside the vexos-ai repo directory (no ~/.claude, ~/.config, ~/.local/share, dconf, /etc). Do not read or write other repos.
- Never read, print or open credential files or tokens.
- Do not run anything inside the user's live GNOME session. Use the nested headless shell under target/ only.
- No nixos-rebuild, just rebuild, install, or sudo.
- No git writes, and do not stage anything. The user commits with GitHub Desktop.
- Downloads into /nix/store are allowed. Tree copies go in a fresh directory under target/, with no `rm -rf`. Run the copy and the build as separate commands.
- New files are untracked, so nix checks may not see them. Run nix checks on a `path:` copy and say so. Ask the user to tick the new files in GitHub Desktop.
- If CLAUDE.md or a hook asks for extra steps, follow this scope rule first and say what you skipped.

### Verification standard

- Run what applies: cargo build --all-targets, cargo test, clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, fmt --check, nix build, checks.policy, checks.contract, checks.core, checks.panel, checks.module, checks.extension, scripts/preflight.sh.
- Say which Rust version you used. CI pins 1.95.0.
- Report only what ran, with exit codes. Use "–" for anything not run. Say what ran on a copy of the tree.
- Mutation-check any new safety test: break the rule, confirm a test fails.
- Tier 3 changes (safety, core, view-model, extension, policy, contract, public interfaces) need the independent reviewer subagent. Fix its findings and run it again on the fixes. Write "Review approved" only if the final run passed. A self-review is labelled "self-review only".
- Finish every item with ONE commit message in the project's commit format. The user commits everything uncommitted in one go, so the message covers all uncommitted work.

### Safety rules that must never be weakened

- Modes pinned (Claude: default or plan, OpenCode: build). The allow-list resets anything else.
- Approval cards offer only Approve once and Deny once. "Always allow" is dropped.
- Nothing is auto-approved. Timeouts, cancels, closes and disconnects deny.
- `Composer::submit` is the only way user-typed text is sent. `check_usage` is the only other sender and sends only the constant `/usage`. Notification drafts need a Send click.
- Agent text is untrusted. It never becomes markup, a command, a path or a setting.
- Nothing in the repo reads Claude's login file or token or calls private endpoints.
- The panel never runs a command that applies system changes. Applying changes stays a terminal action: `just rebuild`.
- The managed policy (nix/policy.nix) only changes through an item that says so.
- An approval request whose card would show more than 16 KiB (counted after escaping) is denied at once and cannot be approved in the panel. Its content is never shown, not even cut. (B3b)
- An approval card shows control and hidden characters as `\u{hex}` and never strips or normalises text, so the command shown is the command that runs. (B3c)

  **Where this list differs from the note (user to approve with the list):**
  1. The note's `ui` setting (`window` default, `shell`) comes back as a TEMPORARY dev switch: the GTK panel stays installed and untouched until B13, then the switch and the GTK panel go (A4: the extension is required, no fallback).
  2. The helper uses a NEW bus name, `io.github.victorytek.VexosAssistant.Helper`, not the GTK panel's name. Reason: the GTK panel owns the old name and its activation file until B13, and the only reason to keep the old name (notification clicks) is gone with the watchers (A9).
  3. The process-id check (A3 condition 1) is required, not optional. Honest limit: the helper checks that the caller's connection is the one owning `org.gnome.Shell`, that its uid is the user's, and that the process behind it is `gnome-shell` (from `GetConnectionCredentials`, then the `/proc/<pid>/exe` link). Other extensions run inside the same process, so this proves "it is the Shell", not "it is our extension". The note said this too.
  4. Numbers from the Phase 0 results replace the note's: a reply or approval card is shown at most 16 KiB (after escaping), not 64 KiB; a `Send` is at most 60,000 bytes, not 72 KiB (the input holds 65,535 bytes).
  5. Approval cards also escape the hidden characters the E4 fix added (tag characters, variation selectors, U+2060-2064), not only control and bidi characters.
  6. The helper registers NO `diagnose-*` actions: with the watchers gone nothing triggers a draft in Shell mode. The draft code in the view-model stays. Say if you want them registered.
  7. Still open: the D-Bus crate (B4a); how the helper learns `usage_on_launch` (B9).

  **Private socket versus bus methods (A9; done here, nothing built):** The bus design needs `Send` and `Decide` on the bus, protected by the sender check on every call. The socket design (`Open()` returns one end of a socketpair; everything else runs on it) takes `Send` and `Decide` off the bus and hides the traffic from bus monitors. Against a hostile OTHER PROCESS the sender check already refuses every call, so the socket adds only confidentiality (a same-user process may be able to read the conversation off the bus; unconfirmed whether the real session bus allows monitoring). Against a hostile EXTENSION (same process as the Shell) neither helps, because it can call `Open()` and get the socket. Against a fake helper neither helps (B6c deals with it). The socket costs a framing protocol, fd passing in GJS (unconfirmed it works from an extension), a parser inside the privileged Shell, and harder tests. Verdict: build the bus methods first, behind a thin transport layer (a Rust trait in the helper, one JS module in the extension), so a socket can replace it later; revisit if bus monitoring turns out to work on the VM (B12 checks it).

(3) **dbus 0.9.12 + crossroads + dbus-tokio**: needs C libdbus-1 (or the `vendored` feature), edition 2018, dbus-tokio last released 2023-03-09; the least attractive. - [~] **B4b** — implemented 2026-11-01 (independent review PASS; see the end of this entry). New crate `crates/vexos-ai-helper` (workspace member; `gio` and `glib` 0.22, already locked; no new external crate; `Cargo.lock` gains the crate's own entry): `gate.rs` (pure rules), `peers.rs` (what the bus and `/proc` say about a caller), `bus.rs` (gio binding), `interface.xml` (the ten methods, no properties, no signals), `main.rs` (owns `io.github.victorytek.VexosAssistant.Helper`; exits when no accepted `Open` comes within 15 s or the bus goes away; every accepted call is answered `NotReady`: no session, nothing is sent). The user's two additions are done. (1) ProcessFD: D-Bus spec revision 0.42 (2023-08-21) added `ProcessFD` to `GetConnectionCredentials` ('safer than ProcessID, as the latter is subject to re-use attacks, while the FD cannot be recycled'); dbus-daemon has it from 1.15.8/1.16.0 (the sandbox proof returned it on 1.16.2), dbus-broker from release 34, NixOS's default is dbus-broker, the kernel needs 6.5 (this machine runs 7.3). The helper uses the descriptor to say which process it is: it reads `Pid:` from `/proc/self/fdinfo/<fd>` (-1 once exited), then `/proc/<pid>/exe`, then the fdinfo again and requires the same live pid; the bus's ProcessID, when present, must equal it; no descriptor means the call is refused. Not documented anywhere I could find: a safe way to read `/proc/<pid>/exe` through a pidfd; the read, re-read pattern rests on the kernel behaviour that `Pid:` is -1 after exit (read in the kernel master source only). (2) Every failed lookup refuses: missing user id, no descriptor, dead or changed process, disagreeing ids, unreadable, non-UTF-8, relative or `(deleted)` program path. Caller check (every call): sender is the current owner of `org.gnome.Shell`, same user id (own id read from `/proc/self/status`, because `/proc/self` is owned by 65534 inside a build sandbox), program file name exactly `gnome-shell` or `.gnome-shell-wrapped`. Differences from the plan text: no identity cache at all (a process can exec another program and keep its connection), the name is requested with `RequestName` not `bus_own_name` (with the bus gone gio calls the lost-name callback with no connection and gio-rs unwraps it, which aborts), and no `NameLost` subscription (the name is not replaceable). Sandbox proof first, as asked: a throw-away derivation ran a private `dbus-daemon` in the Nix sandbox (works; fallback `gio::TestDBus` not needed). Tests: 29 unit tests (gate 15, peers 12, bus 2) and ONE integration test running 19 named scenarios on a private `dbus-daemon` the test starts itself, with a stand-in Shell, a stranger and a separate child process (`CARGO_BIN_EXE_vexos-ai-helper-fakecaller`, built only with `--features testing`): the stranger is refused for all ten methods; the Shell passes for all ten and reaches a recording handler with typed arguments; the Shell under the wrong program, an empty program list, a child that is not the Shell, a child that owns the Shell's name but runs the wrong program (isolates the process rule) and the same child once its program is allowed; no owner, then the owner followed through release and takeover, and an owner that existed before the helper started; wrong arguments never reach the handler and exactly 60,000 bytes passes whole; errors never carry the caller's text; the object has exactly the ten methods (checked on the introspection too) and no properties; unknown methods, objects and interfaces; exit timer (no `Open`, accepted `Open`, refused `Open`); name already owned; dropping the helper releases its name; the bus going away. 37 mutations on the gate, peers and bus: 35 killed first time; of the 2 survivors, one (dropping an explicit connection close) showed the close was redundant and was removed, and one (the gate's own owner check after the async lookup, behind the pre-filter that already refuses a stranger) stays: it only matters if the Shell's name changes hands during the lookup, which a test cannot provoke without timing luck. Build: new `checks.<system>.helper` in `flake.nix` (glib, pkg-config, dbus; clippy `-D warnings`), `scripts/preflight.sh` and `CLAUDE.md` updated; the check passes in the Nix sandbox on a `path:` copy (the crate is untracked). Not tested: two different real users, the real GNOME Shell as the caller, a hostile extension inside the Shell, the owner changing mid-lookup. INDEPENDENT REVIEW: PASS, no CRITICAL finding; it could not find a way for a non-Shell, wrong-user or wrong-program caller to reach the handler, and it confirmed that the Nix check runs the scenarios inside the sandbox. Four RECOMMENDED findings: (1) `Open` returned a `generation` value the plan did not list: removed, `Open` replies nothing (the generation arrives with `Decide` in B4e, with an interface change then); (2) a code comment named `bus_own_name` where `bus_own_name_on_connection` is the function that aborts: fixed; (3) the test caller could carry on as a stranger if the Shell's name was already owned: it now asserts it owns it: fixed; (4) the dev shell (`nix develop`) has no `dbus-daemon`, so the scenarios pass there only because this host has `/usr/bin/dbus-daemon`: NOT changed, it needs a `flake.nix` edit the plan did not list, waiting for the user's yes (add `dbus` to the dev shell). Honest limit to repeat in any report: the program rule matches the program FILE NAME (`gnome-shell` or `.gnome-shell-wrapped`), so it does not prove 'the gnome-shell binary': a same-user process running a binary renamed like that passes whenever the Shell's name is free (same-user code is outside this check by A3). On the real session bus the reviewer saw `ProcessFD` for `org.gnome.Shell` and the process name `.gnome-shell-wr`; whether a same-user process can read the real Shell's `/proc/<pid>/exe` is not verified (the reviewer's own sandbox denied it) and goes on the VM checklist (B12): if it cannot, the helper would refuse the Shell. Forward note for B4d: each Shell call waits for its own lookup, so the order in which calls reach the handler rests on GLib running the waiting calls in arrival order; B4d's `Edited`-before-`Send` rules depend on it and need a test. Original: (Needs: B3, B4a) New headless crate `vexos-ai-helper`: owns `Session`, `Conversation` and `Composer`, no window, new bus name, `serde` on the display types it sends (additive). Exits when no `Open()` follows activation. Needs core API only as-is; if a core change is needed, stop and ask.

Fix: drop headers only before the first `@@`. Also: adding or removing a final newline does not show on a card. Tier 3 (approval content); needs a plan first.

Bash does not split words on them, so `cp a<NBSP>b /dst` looks like two words and is one. The set is shared with the log sanitizer, and U+202F appears in Claude's own reset text (`usage.rs`), so the recommendation is to escape them on cards ONLY, not in logs. The tests that now say U+00A0, U+200A, U+202F and U+205F are left alone would change with it. Needs the user's yes.
